主要内容: An internal audit by Ernst & Young found the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) failed to properly track over $800 million in construction projects, Politico reported. The audit identified deficiencies in documentation for millions of dollars in property and equipment. DLA concurred with the findings, acknowledging a lack of complete documentation for military construction and real property. The audit also revealed at least $465 million in misstatements for construction projects, including those financed for the Army Corps of Engineers or other defense agencies. Insufficient documentation was found for around $384 million in spending for "in progress" projects. The Pentagon estimates its department-wide audit would cost $367 million in 2018 and another $551 million to fix problems. About 1,200 auditors are participating in the process. The audit also disclosed the Army had 39 Black Hawk helicopters not properly recorded in its system, and the Air Force identified hundreds of structures not in its real property system.
